methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TurbineOne Establishes Virginia Headquarters, Launches T1 Edgeworks Innovation Center - The AI Journal
signals.signal_reading: TurbineOne's defense AI headquarters and innovation center in NoVA signals deepening concentration of specialized AI capability in the metro corridor, reinforcing the region's gravity well for defense-adjacent AI talent and capital while widening the capability gap with other Virginia regions.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's young workforce facing AI pressure suggests platform-driven automation is creating shallow, distributed adoption pressure across metro markets—workers adapting to AI tools rather than building deep technical capability, consistent with consumer-grade AI diffusion.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents intentional capability-building in historically underserved regions, potentially enabling distributed deep skills development if training emphasizes technical fluency rather than surface-level tool use.

signals.title: Norfolk Southern deploys AI system to catch wheel defects before they break - The Business Journals
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Southern's deployment of AI defect detection systems signals enterprise-grade deep capability concentrating in Hampton Roads' industrial and logistics corridors, but likely represents vendor-supplied solutions rather than indigenous technical capacity building.

signals.title: RC-RV partners with ed2go to launch innovative, on-demand workforce training programs - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's partnership with ed2go for on-demand workforce training signals platform-mediated skill distribution, but the emphasis on 'on-demand' and turnkey solutions suggests shallow adoption mechanics rather than deep technical capability development in the region.
